rationale: validation_status is fail and analyzer flags a dead_check (SR5) that never emits FAIL on any mutant or baseline, confirmed by the SR5_stuck_at_signal mutant which fully mirrors the naive baseline (infected=false, suspect_nodes=[], empty output) but still shows SR5 PASS in both baseline_run and vulnerable_run stdout. This is a tautological check providing no discriminative security value, and per rules a dead_check issue requires evaluation_framework revision. FR3/FR4 being untested by mutants is a lower-severity gap that should also be addressed but is secondary to the dead SR5 check.
revision_instructions: SR5 in evaluate.py currently always PASSes regardless of the submission's actual infected/suspect_nodes/primary_output_affected values, making it a vacuous tautology (confirmed: it PASSes even on the fully naive/empty-style submission that fails SR1-SR4). Rewrite SR5 as an independently meaningful check: rather than re-testing the submission, SR5 should be a fixture/self-test that verifies the shipped naive baseline submission (infected=false, suspect_nodes=[]) itself fails SR1 through SR4 when run through the same grading logic used for participant submissions. Implement this as an internal harness check invoked once (e.g., at evaluator startup or as its own test) that loads the naive baseline fixture, runs check_sr1 through check_sr4 against it, and asserts that all four return FAIL; SR5 itself should FAIL if any of SR1-SR4 unexpectedly PASS on that naive baseline. This makes SR5 an evaluator self-consistency guarantee instead of a no-op. Additionally, strengthen mutation/differential coverage for FR3 and FR4: add or confirm mutant cases where infected=true but suspect_nodes=[] (or infected=false but suspect_nodes non-empty) to exercise FR3, and a case where infected=true but primary_output_affected names an invalid/nonexistent port to exercise FR4, and verify evaluate.py actually FAILs these behaviorally against the submitted JSON fields rather than skipping them silently.
